candidates.title: 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts Ran a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories, Then Wiped the Logs Nov 12, 2026 Supply Chain / Cloud Security Starting Tuesday, an attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer in repositories those accounts could write to, according to Aikido Security, a security software company. The stealer is built to take the secrets and cloud credentials that a repository's CI workflows can reach. It ran in at least 1,806 repositories, where the attacker has likely collected those credentials, the company says. Each attack started with a pull request titled docs: dependency audit notes, opened from a branch named wfx-docs to test whether the account could write to the repository. These test pull requests were opened in 61,764 repositories, and the stealer followed in some of them. After pushing the stealer, the attacker usually reverted the change within minutes. Where the stealer ran, its logs were deleted, usually along with the run itself. In those repositories, every secret and cloud role available to the workflows should be treated as compromised. ...

Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely Nov 12, 2026 Vulnerability / Web Security A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2 , can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618 , it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux. An attacker who can reach the server needs no authentication to exploit the flaw and could take full control of the server process, the Linux vendor says. It rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported. ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients Nov 12, 2026 Malware / Endpoint Security ConnectWise has taken the precautionary step of disabling five third-party extensions in partner environments following reports of unauthorized access . In an advisory posted on its site, the company said there is no evidence that the incident involves a compromise of its infrastructure or a vulnerability in the ScreenConnect software. "Our initial assessment suggests the activity may involve a threat actor's abuse of independent third-party extensions installed in partner environments," it said . "We are continuing to validate this assessment. The initial access method and full scope remain under investigation." ConnectWise has identified about 400 partner environments with at least one of the third-party extensions installed. It also emphasized that the presence of the extensions alone does not indicate or establish compromise. eMudhra Revokes 8 More CAs It Previously Declared Unaffected by Key Compromise Nov 11, 2026 Web Security / Cryptography The in-house Python script behind eMudhra's October key compromise has now cost the company 8 more of its intermediate certificate authorities (CAs), even though it did not weaken their keys. Each intermediate CA has its own private key, which the company uses to sign the certificates it issues. The 8 intermediate CAs compromised in October had a different problem: a single line in the script cut each of their keys to one byte, the company said this week. The script also retrieved the RSA keys of the 8 newly revoked CAs from the company's hardware security modules (HSMs). The company says it cannot show that the keys were handled as required by its own rules. It revoked the CAs late last week. The company had called those CAs unaffected. "The RSA issuers went through a different path as per our assessment of the code and are therefore not impacted," it wrote on Mozilla's bug tracker on October 19. Microsoft Patches 1,259 Flaws, Including Exploited Outlook Bug That May Expose NTLMv2 Hashes Nov 11, 2026 Vulnerability / Windows Security Microsoft on Tuesday released patches for a total of 1,259 vulnerabilities spanning its software portfolio, the second consecutive month where the patch volume has exceeded 1,000 flaws. These cover 726 flaws in Windows, 174 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 59 in SQL Server, 53 in Developer Tools, and 27 in SharePoint Server. The patches also include 165 non-Microsoft-issued CVE identifiers. More than 500 flaws relate to elevation of privilege, followed by remote code execution and information disclosure bugs. With the latest round of fixes, Microsoft has addressed over 5,100 CVEs this year alone, according to Satnam Narang, senior staff research engineer at Tenable. Of these, a Moderate-severity security flaw in Microsoft Outlook ( CVE-2026-124194 , CVSS score: 6.5) has been flagged as actively exploited by Microsoft.
